title: Time-lapse imaging of Drosophila testis for monitoring actin dynamics and sperm release
author: Kapoor, Dubey, et al.

steps.title: Prepare 1× PBS Imaging Buffer
steps.instruction: Make 10× PBS according to Sambrook and Russell, adjust pH to 7.47, dilute 1:10 with distilled water to obtain 1× PBS, re‑check pH and adjust to 7.4 if needed.

steps.title: Reconstitute and Aliquot Drug Stocks
steps.instruction: Dissolve each small‑molecule reagent in DMSO or distilled water following the manufacturer’s instructions; prepare working (bath) concentrations in 1× PBS as follows: Rockout 200 µM, SMIFH2 25 µM, CK‑666 250 µM, Latrunculin A 5 µM, Latrunculin B 10 µM, Taxol 10 µM, Colchicine 10 µM, Cytochalasin D 20 µM (also 2.5 µM for titration), Jasplakinolide 50 µM. Aliquot stocks and store per manufacturer guidelines (PBS and drug solutions stable for a few months).

steps.title: Fabricate Glass‑Bottom Petri Dishes (Overnight)
steps.instruction: Create reusable imaging chambers by drilling an 8 mm hole in the bottom of a 35 mm plastic Petri dish and sealing it with a wax‑petroleum jelly plug.

substeps.instruction: Drill an 8 mm round hole through the bottom of a 35 mm plastic Petri dish using a motorized drill.
Mix myristic acid wax and petroleum jelly in a 9:4 (w/w) ratio and keep the mixture at 70 °C on a heating block.
Line the heating block with tissue paper and arrange multiple square coverslips (18 mm or 22 mm, #0 or #1 thickness) about 2 inches apart on the paper.
Using a paintbrush, draw a square wax outline around the drilled hole on the outer surface of the dish.
Place the dish (hole centered) on the heated block directly over a coverslip; gently press the coverslip onto the dish with a piece of tissue paper so excess wax flows onto the tissue.
Allow the wax to solidify (few minutes; color changes from transparent to translucent).
Remove the dish from the block and store it in a box; repeat to make as many dishes as needed.
Wash the inner surface of each dish and its lid with distilled water using a squirt bottle.
Place dishes and lids in a cell‑culture hood with UV light and airflow on, leaving the hood slightly ajar to avoid pressure buildup; leave overnight for sterilization.
Next day, store the sterilized dishes in a box at ~23 °C for long‑term use (months).

steps.title: Apply Poly‑L‑Lysine and Prepare Imaging Cavity
steps.instruction: Just before imaging, coat the coverslip surface with poly‑L‑lysine, wash, and add PBS or drug solution as the live‑imaging medium.

substeps.instruction: Gently wipe the coverslip surface with lint‑free tissue paper and place the dish on clean tissue.
Add 50–80 µL of poly‑L‑lysine into the cavity and let it sit undisturbed for 15–20 min (use this time to set imaging parameters and dissect testes).
Remove the poly‑L‑lysine with a micropipette.
Wash the cavity three times with ~50 µL of 1× PBS each to eliminate residual poly‑L‑lysine.
Add fresh 1× PBS (80–100 µL) to the cavity as the live‑imaging medium, or add the appropriate drug working solution prepared in 1× PBS.
Ensure DMSO concentration in the final imaging solution is ≤0.8 % (dilute stock at least 100‑fold). Use freshly prepared working solutions.

Effective inhibitory concentrations to use (if drug treatment is desired): Rockout 200 µM; SMIFH2 25 µM; Latrunculin A 5 µM; Latrunculin B 10 µM; Cytochalasin D 2.5 µM and 20 µM; Jasplakinolide 50 µM; Colchicine 10 µM; Taxol 10 µM; CK‑666 250 µM.

description: F-actin dynamics is essential for cellular and tissue morphogenesis, as it forms the underlying basis for various cellular processes such as shaping the plasma membrane, cell migration, cytokinesis, endocytosis, etc. (Blanchoin et al., 2014)(Skau and Waterman, 2015). Actin and plasma membrane remodelling are closely interlinked, and the causal relationship between them is an active area of recent investigation in cell biology (Kessels and Qualmann, 2021). The process of spermatid maturation and release in Drosophila testis provides an excellent opportunity to study the molecular cell biology of the interplay between F-actin dynamics and membrane sculpting at the tissue and organ level ex vivo. For example, the indentation of the head cyst cell membrane by mature spermatids was shown to induce two different forms of F-actin assembly at distinct time scales using time-lapse confocal imaging from isolated Drosophila testis (Dubey et al., 2016)(Kapoor et al., 2021). This system provided an opportunity to observe subcellular changes in the F-actin dynamics and correlate them with the morphogenetic processes in different genetic backgrounds and in the presence of specific function-blocking reagents, using an inexpensive and straightforward protocol. This protocol specifically describes how to collect 5D (x, y, z, t, and multi-channel) images of F-actin structures associated with the maturing spermatid heads in Drosophila testis at high resolution using a confocal microscope, with minimal equipment and sample preparation. This technique has been standardized using simple 1× Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS) as the culture medium. This improvisation allows the isolated testis to be imaged for an extended period of time (4–6 h) on the confocal microscope, with minimal peristalsis of the tissue.
